newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary sets time limit on wheat export licences.
newsitem.headline: Hungary sets time limit on wheat export licences.

text.p: Hungary's Agriculture Ministry said it will grant unlimited export licences for ordinary and durum wheat exports this year but deliveries have to be made by October 31 the latest.
"We thought it would be more reasonable to set a time, rather than a volume limit on wheat exports," State Secretary Fulop Benedek told Reuters.

Those who are granted an export licence for ordinary wheat will have to deposit 1,500 forints per tonne and the sum will only be reimbursed if they deliver at least 80 percent of the amount in their licence, the ministry said in a statement.
Applications will be accepted from June 23 for durum wheat and July 1 for ordinary wheat, both until September 30, the ministry said.
Some 80 to 82 percent of Hungary's wheat crop is expected to be ordinary wheat, Benedek said.
Benedek said the ministry forecasts a wheat crop of "slightly under five million tonnes" up from last year's official crop figure of 3.9 million tonnes.
He said the actual 1995/96 crop might have been some 200,000 to 300,000 tonnes less than the ministry's original figures although he added they would only be able to readjust the figure by September.
